target_customer: Enterprise security teams (SOCs) wanting to detect attackers inside the network
problem: Attackers who get past the perimeter move laterally unseen. Deception decoys and breadcrumbs let defenders detect and trap them early.
business_model: Enterprise software licenses for MazeRunner and ActiveSOC, plus deception as a service

founders.name: Gadi Evron
founders.background_notes: Aggregators list other co-founders (Imri Goldberg, Dean Sysman and others) inconsistently

exit.reason: Private equity turnaround and growth firm acquired the company and planned a Denver headquarters

competitors.name: TrapX Security
competitors.what: DeceptionGrid, fake assets that trigger alerts

competitors.name: Attivo Networks
competitors.what: Deception platform, added AWS support in September 2015

technical_complexity.rationale: Building convincing decoys, breadcrumbs and a management console is standard enterprise security engineering with hard parts around realism and low false positives.

defensibility.rationale: Several competitors built similar products at the same time, and differentiation rested on execution and a claim of catching nation-state APTs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large vendors did not buy Cymmetria. Rival Attivo Networks was later bought by SentinelOne in 2022 for a reported $616M, per one search result. Cymmetria was bought by a PE turnaround firm in 2019.

market_need_then: Gartner called deception a key emerging security technology around 2015, and breaches of perimeter defenses were common, which created interest in internal detection.

branding.domain_note: Uses cymmetria.com; the site now returns 403 to fetchers

identity.voice_and_tone: Offensive-minded security framing: hunt attackers, shift the asymmetry to defenders

branding.brand_signature: MazeRunner product name and the asymmetry tagline

brand_strength.rationale: Product name MazeRunner is memorable but the company name is hard to spell, and no press about the brand itself was found.

outcome_analysis: Cymmetria raised about 10.5 million dollars in 2015, joined the YC Summer 2015 batch and sold deception products to enterprises in a market Gartner flagged as emerging. After the 2015 rounds no later funding was found, and it was acquired by the Stage Fund in September 2019 for an undisclosed price, which looks like a modest outcome with no public valuation.
notes: Company site returned 403 so it is treated as unreadable, not dead. Round amounts come from search summaries of Dark Reading and aggregators; the seed amount rests on a Seedtable page and a NoCamels report seen in a snippet. Series A lead is reported as Sherpa Capital by one source and Rally Ventures by another. A single low quality profile claims a 2023 KELA acquisition, unverified and not recorded. Aggregator totals range 10.6M to 11M. Cymmetria name origin and logo not found.
